decision: A UI that runs inside another application keeps its review surface on its browser mock page, not inside the host. A plugin in a DAW or a Max for Live device lives in the host's window, and that window is the instrument: a built-in review panel has no place there. The template that builds it draws the editor and its mock page with one engine, from the same parameter table, and puts the review surface on the mock only; reviewing the mock reviews the editor.
scope: every page that restates the review rule (interactive first versions ship reviewable) without the host-embedded case: Shop/Maker.md § Interactive deliverables ship reviewable, first; the review-layer kit's README opening line (mount it on a first build); any Specialist page that restates the rule later.
check: each restatement names the case in one sentence, or points at Review Layer for it: a UI that runs inside another application keeps its review surface on its browser mock page, never in the host.
proposed_action: add the host-embedded case to the restatement in one sentence pointing at Review Layer, or replace the restatement with a pointer; an interactive Specialist's Self-Check says the mock page carries the surface for a hosted UI.
rationale: Loudon, 2026-10-21: 'Yes, post the propagate flag for the Maker page's old review rule.' The rule itself on his yes in the VST session: 'Lets fix the rule clash, I like your solution, review on the mockup.' (88bd36fd). That session's finding: a plugin's editor lives in the host's window and cannot carry the review kit; the VST Template draws the editor and its mock from one parameter table and mounts the kit on the mock only (ui.py mock), landed at ff175004.
